long_biography.plain_text:
Matty Zadnikar entered the Eisden coal mine in 1979, following his Slovenian father and grandfather underground. He advanced from gas, air and dust measurement to training mine-rescue teams, while studying technical engineering in evening classes. When Belgium's mines closed, that experience became the foundation for an industrial-safety business.

Zadnikar combined trained personnel, rentable equipment and a patented monitoring system for hazardous industrial work. After the business became part of Total Safety, he redirected its service-and-rental lessons into SeaNet, adapting a US co-ownership model for European clients. He remains the company's founder and executive chairman, overseeing maritime co-ownership, management, brokerage and crew services.
long_biography.html:
Matty Zadnikar entered the Eisden coal mine in 1979, following his Slovenian father and grandfather underground. He advanced from gas, air and dust measurement to training mine-rescue teams, while studying technical engineering in evening classes. When Belgium's mines closed, that experience became the foundation for an industrial-safety business.

Zadnikar combined trained personnel, rentable equipment and a patented monitoring system for hazardous industrial work. After the business became part of Total Safety, he redirected its service-and-rental lessons into SeaNet, adapting a US co-ownership model for European clients. He remains the company's founder and executive chairman, overseeing maritime co-ownership, management, brokerage and crew services.
